THE OBSERVATION
The network sees a 10 x 10 grid. Rows are numbered 0 (top) to 9 (bottom) and columns 0 (left) to 9 (right). The outer ring of cells (row 0, row 9, column 0 and column 9) is a wall border; the playable area is the inner 8 x 8 cells (rows 1-8, columns 1-8).
Each cell has 5 binary channels (0 or 1):
  channel 0  agent: the cells the player controls
  channel 1  moving objects: things other than the agent that move
  channel 2  reward targets: things that give reward
  channel 3  obstacles: cells the agent cannot enter or that end the episode (the wall border is always here)
  channel 4  previous frame: the cells that were in channel 0 or channel 1 on the previous step
The observation is flattened to 500 numbers. Input number i = (row * 10 + column) * 5 + channel; for example input 0 is (row 0, column 0, channel 0), input 4 is (row 0, column 0, channel 4), input 5 is (row 0, column 1, channel 0) and input 499 is (row 9, column 9, channel 4).

THE ACTIONS
The network outputs 5 numbers (logits), one per action; the action is sampled from the softmax of these logits:
  action 0  no-op
  action 1  up (toward row 0)
  action 2  down (toward row 9)
  action 3  left (toward column 0)
  action 4  right (toward column 9)

THE NETWORK
A policy network (multilayer perceptron) with 500 inputs, two hidden layers of 32 units with tanh activations, and 5 outputs:
  h1 = tanh(x' @ W1 + b1)         W1: 500 x 32, b1: 32
  h2 = tanh(h1 @ W2 + b2)         W2: 32 x 32,  b2: 32
  logits = h2 @ W3 + b3           W3: 32 x 5,   b3: 5
Here x' is the transformed observation defined in THE INPUT TRANSFORMATION below, and row j of W1 holds the weights from x'_j (position j of x') to the 32 hidden units; column j of a weight matrix belongs to unit j of the next layer. 17,253 parameters in total. It was trained with reinforcement learning (PPO) to maximise the reward of a game played on this grid.

THE INPUT TRANSFORMATION
Before the first layer, the 500 observation numbers x (indexed as above) are transformed into x' in 1 step, applied in this order (v is the vector before a step, v' the vector after it; the first step starts from v = x and the last step gives x'). The network was rewritten so that it computes exactly the same function of x as before the transformation:
  step 1, permutation by rule: v'_j = v_{p(j)} for j = 0..499 (row j of W1 holds the weights of original input p(j)), where p(j) is computed as follows. Start with x = j. Apply the 64 rounds listed below in order; round r does x ← (a_r · x + c_r) mod 512 and then x ← x XOR (x >> 3) (bitwise exclusive-or of x with x shifted right by 3 bits, i.e. with floor(x / 8)). If the result after all 64 rounds is 500 or more, apply all 64 rounds again to that result, and repeat until the result is less than 500; that result is p(j). Every round is a bijection of 0..511, so p is a permutation of 0..499. The rounds (a_r odd): round 1: a = 427, c = 511; round 2: a = 473, c = 482; round 3: a = 173, c = 438; round 4: a = 385, c = 332; round 5: a = 87, c = 159; round 6: a = 257, c = 326; round 7: a = 451, c = 168; round 8: a = 179, c = 234; round 9: a = 337, c = 196; round 10: a = 367, c = 394; round 11: a = 15, c = 116; round 12: a = 167, c = 151; round 13: a = 91, c = 111; round 14: a = 45, c = 500; round 15: a = 291, c = 391; round 16: a = 449, c = 486; round 17: a = 97, c = 39; round 18: a = 381, c = 495; round 19: a = 61, c = 108; round 20: a = 391, c = 96; round 21: a = 443, c = 286; round 22: a = 469, c = 277; round 23: a = 411, c = 116; round 24: a = 119, c = 439; round 25: a = 93, c = 214; round 26: a = 85, c = 168; round 27: a = 65, c = 164; round 28: a = 355, c = 286; round 29: a = 275, c = 459; round 30: a = 45, c = 303; round 31: a = 175, c = 246; round 32: a = 347, c = 362; round 33: a = 403, c = 438; round 34: a = 179, c = 234; round 35: a = 31, c = 333; round 36: a = 73, c = 142; round 37: a = 121, c = 227; round 38: a = 247, c = 37; round 39: a = 31, c = 457; round 40: a = 445, c = 119; round 41: a = 381, c = 106; round 42: a = 157, c = 129; round 43: a = 405, c = 417; round 44: a = 359, c = 198; round 45: a = 181, c = 156; round 46: a = 389, c = 338; round 47: a = 463, c = 175; round 48: a = 131, c = 15; round 49: a = 229, c = 300; round 50: a = 339, c = 75; round 51: a = 233, c = 63; round 52: a = 337, c = 70; round 53: a = 255, c = 370; round 54: a = 331, c = 2; round 55: a = 227, c = 343; round 56: a = 259, c = 128; round 57: a = 313, c = 117; round 58: a = 411, c = 288; round 59: a = 317, c = 81; round 60: a = 431, c = 460; round 61: a = 255, c = 203; round 62: a = 87, c = 281; round 63: a = 333, c = 338; round 64: a = 321, c = 428.

QUESTION. The weights below belong to one policy network that was trained with reinforcement learning to play a game on this grid. Which game was it trained on? Work from the weights. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run. This is a single response.

Answer in this order:
Observations: <what you see in the weights: for each input channel, where in the grid its weights are large or show structure and what that suggests; what the output layer and its biases show about the actions; quote the weights you rely on>
Reasoning: <which kinds of game fit these observations, which are ruled out, and why>
Game: <the game, as specifically as you can; if it resembles a well-known game, give that game's name>
Description: <what the agent does and what gives reward, in one or two sentences>
Confidence: <0-100>%
